methodology: Empirical benchmark across 500,000 monthly web pages comparing raw HTML DOM prompt feeding (42,000 tokens/page) against Fit-Markdown pruning (Crawl4AI / Firecrawl) and Accessibility-Tree DOM distillation (Browser-Use / Stagehand).

repositories.name: Firecrawl
repositories.primary_win: Turns entire dynamic JS websites into clean LLM-ready Markdown or structured JSON schemas via /scrape, /crawl, and /extract endpoints
repositories.primary_caveat: Cloud credit consumption scales rapidly on deep recursive site crawls without URL path regex filters

repositories.name: Browser-Use
repositories.primary_win: 118k+ star Python agent SDK that distills interactive DOM elements into indexed bounding boxes and accessibility trees for multi-step web actions
repositories.primary_caveat: Multi-step vision+DOM loops can consume 8k-15k tokens per task without max_actions_per_step and DOM pruning rules

repositories.name: Crawl4AI
repositories.primary_win: 85.6k+ star Apache-2.0 async Playwright crawler with BM25 Fit-Markdown heuristic pruning that strips 96% of boilerplate HTML tokens
repositories.primary_caveat: Local headless Chromium pools require explicit memory-limit recycling to avoid zombie browser processes under high concurrency

repositories.name: Stagehand
repositories.primary_win: Hybrid Playwright + AI SDK (act, extract, observe) with deterministic DOM action caching that cuts repeat workflow token spend by 54%
repositories.primary_caveat: TypeScript-first SDK; Python teams typically prefer Browser-Use or Crawl4AI for native async integration

repositories.name: Skyvern
repositories.primary_win: Vision-LLM + DOM swarm agent built for complex enterprise form filling, 2FA/TOTP flows, and brittle procurement portals
repositories.primary_caveat: Vision-first screenshot analysis adds ~250ms per step compared to pure DOM accessibility-tree extraction
